transcript: Every month, money just appears in millions of bank accounts. No envelope. No queue. No guy at a desk taking a cut. In Madhya Pradesh, a scheme called Ladli Behna sends eligible women a fixed amount, every single month. It didn't always work like this. Welfare money used to travel down a chain of offices before it reached you. Every hand on that chain was a place for some of it to leak. So India rebuilt the pipe. Step one, bank accounts for millions who never had one. Step two, Aadhaar. A twelve digit ID tied to your fingerprints and your irises. Step three, link them. Now the government doesn't need your account number. [short pause] Here's the twist. The treasury pays your Aadhaar number, and a national switch figures out which bank you're in. [short pause] Your body is basically the address. So every month, money just appears. [deadpan] Unless you're a penguin. No fingerprints.
